items.name: ILSpy
items.summary: .NET decompiler praised for inspecting NuGet packages and uncovering implementation gaps.
items.why_included: A first-hand workflow endorsement connects decompilation to finding actionable bugs.
items.evidence: A commenter finds using ILSpy to inspect NuGet implementations effective and says the workflow reveals bugs or gaps in their own packages.

evidence_sources.author: sreekanth850
evidence_sources.excerpt: With C#, whenever codex need some info about the packages we use, it just use ILSpy to decompile the nuget instead of checking the docs. its much effective though. Even in my own packages, it use to gave back the bugs or gaps that i need to patch up.

items.name: Aeneas
items.source_story_title: Compiling Rust to readable C with Eurydice
items.summary: Rust verification toolchain translating programs into functional models for proof assistants.
items.why_included: An explicit recommendation names Aeneas among the Rust verification projects worth exploring.
items.evidence: A commenter highly recommends AeneasVerif projects and specifically names Aeneas alongside Scylla and Charon.

evidence_sources.author: weinzierl
evidence_sources.excerpt: I highly recommend checking out the other projects from AeneasVerif (and Jonathan Protzenko). Scylla is kind of Eurydice's dual. But also Charon and the eponymous Aeneas.

items.name: OpenSCAD
items.source_story_title: OpenSCAD the Programmers Solid 3D CAD Modeller
items.summary: Code-driven 3D modeller praised for productive geometric designs and fabric printing.
items.why_included: Fresh first-hand praise demonstrates practical use, and its previous report is outside the cooldown.
items.evidence: Jeff Barr reports great results using OpenSCAD for 3D printing on fabric and says he finds its functional model efficient and productive.

evidence_sources.author: jeffbarr
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have been using OpenSCAD to create cool geometric designs for 3D printing on fabric, with great results. The functional model is likely unfamiliar to most developers, but I have found that I can be efficient and productive with it.
